text: To construct a parallelogram equal to a given triangle in a given rectilinear angle. Let $ABC$ be the given triangle, and $D$ the given rectilinear angle. So it is required to construct a parallelogram equal to triangle $ABC$ in the rectilinear angle $D$.
Let $BC$ have been cut in half at $E$ [Prop.~1.10],
And let (angle) $CEF$, equal to angle $D$,  have been constructed at the point $E$ on the straight-line $EC$ [Prop.~1.23].
And let $AG$ have been drawn through $A$ parallel to $EC$ [Prop.~1.31],
and let $CG$ have been drawn through $C$ parallel to $EF$ [Prop.~1.31].
And since $BE$ is equal to $EC$, triangle $ABE$ is also equal to triangle $AEC$.
assertion: triangle ABE is equal to triangle AEC

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: triangle $ABE$ is also equal to triangle $AEC$

text: For they are on the equal bases, $BE$ and $EC$,
assertion: triangles ABE and AEC are on the equal bases BE and EC

text: and between the same parallels, $BC$ and $AG$ [Prop.~1.38].
assertion: triangles ABE and AEC are between the same parallels BC and AG

text: Thus, triangle $ABC$ is double (the area) of triangle $AEC$.
assertion: triangle ABC is double the area of triangle AEC

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: triangle $ABC$ is double (the area) of triangle $AEC$

text: And parallelogram $FECG$ is also double (the area) of triangle $AEC$.
assertion: parallelogram FECG is double the area of triangle AEC

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: parallelogram $FECG$ is also double (the area) of triangle $AEC$

text: For it has the same base as ($AEC$),
assertion: FECG has the same base as triangle AEC

text: and is between the same parallels  as ($AEC$) [Prop.~1.41].
assertion: FECG is between the same parallels as triangle AEC

text: Thus, parallelogram $FECG$ is equal to triangle $ABC$.
assertion: parallelogram FECG is equal to triangle ABC

text: ($FECG$) also has the angle $CEF$ equal to the given (angle) $D$.
assertion: FECG has angle CEF equal to the given angle D

spans.label: assertion
spans.text: ($FECG$) also has the angle $CEF$ equal to the given (angle) $D$

text: Thus, parallelogram $FECG$,  equal to the given triangle $ABC$, has been constructed in the angle $CEF$, which is equal to $D$. (Which is) the very thing it was required to do.
